questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to go to Asia, and found Korea to be the perfect place to go. Safe, fun and a good hub for further traveling.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing! Would 100% recommend.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say quite easy, it always takes time to figure out a new country, university system, metro etc - but it's all worth it. Being unsure about stuff is a part of the process, and it always works out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a mentor could, which was nice! I recommend joining that, it's essentially just Korean students who have dinner, party and help you out with stuff. You also get to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Covered all my needs.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, used Simplespaces as i'd seen other student reports talk about. Was 45ish minutes on public transport, but all in all great. They hosted trips, events and we all lived in the same cute neighborhood.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a bit more expensive, but still quite cheap compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought it was Ok. You can't except to get all the courses you want when on exchange, and you don't really know how each course will be either, so that might be a good thing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You show how interested you are in a course by betting an amount of points, and essentially if there are more students who want the course than there are spots, then it goes to those with the most points allocated. Sounds very difficult, but it's fully manageable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have a global lounge and I guess the mentors as well, but I figured it out myself. They send out emails with detailed guides on all of this, including Youtube videos with walk-throughs.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Courses changed a lot from 2024 to 2025, so all the pre-registered courses I had found which looked interesting from last semester were gone.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did two courses at GSIS which is essentially masters/phd students for students from aboard, mostly US and Chinese students. Here the level was substantially lower than at home. I did another course at the Public Policy department with purely phd students and mostly just Koreans, this on the other hand was more demanding, and also more interesting. In general I've heard that the public policy department is great, so take courses there if you can.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Graduate, which covers both MA & PhD, but mostly MA students in my courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They're not all great in english, neither the students nor the students. This is just something you have to deal with, in some courses you'll be better off reading the slides than listening. Also you have to show up for at least 2/3 of the lectures to pass.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to tax policy, economics of international development, diplomatic law & practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to tax policy, good professor at the public policy department. Also if you want more demanding courses 7000+ level courses are usually PhD only.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not much, in general stuff is cheaper, but if you travel and go out you will spend a decent amount of money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The cafeterias at uni are really cheap, and good! Try the spicy pork bowl!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got what I wanted, essentially meet people early and then do my own thing with the people I met. For me it was great.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were loads of clubs, trips etc. I didn't do much organized stuff after the first two weeks.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to some sporting events!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I travelled as much as possible, both in Korea before I got my ARC (essentially residence card, you need this to leave the country, and it can take 2 ish months), and outside. I did a weekend trip in Beijing which was amazing, one of the highlights of my trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It's always a bit rough at first, especially being so far away, but after a couple weeks you wont think about it!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's difficult, but try to talk to them in class if you have any classes with them. They can be quite shy, especially because their english is not always the best, but they're very nice people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The no talking on public transport was a bit odd, but now I love it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They're very polite people, such as standing in line.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Sinchon, where Yonsei is, is a cool area filled with bars, restaurants, karaokespots etc. Spend some time here after lectures, enjoy!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing comes to mind

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Asia was amazing, so different yet now it feels so like home. It's a transformative experience I would recommend to anyone.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The august heat was actually unbearable, but two weeks into september it got better!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you're still debating going to Asia, Korea or Yonsei I'd say do it 100%. You will surely have a great time, meets loads of fun people and make friends from all over the world.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
